newsitem.title: USA: Stone sets funding plan, may sell assets.
newsitem.headline: Stone sets funding plan, may sell assets.

text.p: Stone Container Corp said Tuesday it is implementing a $700 million funding program and is considering "various options" for the sale or monetization of certain assets.
If assets are sold or monetized, debt could be reduced significantly, said the paper, packaging and pulp company.
Stone Container said its funding program is designed to address its near-term capital, financing and debt amortization needs.

The program includes an offering of $250 million of senior subordinated debt due 2002, an underwritten $200 million senior secured term loan due 2003, and a $95 million mortgage financing commitment on certain of the company's box plants.
The program also includes financing in Germany totalling 170 million marks ($100 million) due through 2004, and a $16 million tax-exempt financing with a 30-year maturity.
In addition, inventory reductions associated with mill downtime are expected to reduce inventories by more than $50 million in the near term, available for liquidity, the company said.

"This significant program immediately addresses the financing and debt amortization needs of our company in the near term and restores appropriate liquidity for the company," Roger Stone, chairman, said in a statement.

"These fundings will provide the company, along with our current lines of credit, with cash availability of almost $900 million, while at the same time bringing the company's subordinated capital base to over $1 billion," Randolph Read, chief financial officer, added.
Stone Container said it intends to schedule a meeting with its lenders under its credit agreement, at which it will present various amendments to that agreement.
Those amendments are expected to include obtaining approval regarding use of proceeds from most of the new financings. It is expected most of the financings will be completed by June 30, it added.
Regarding possible asset sales or monetization of certain assets, Stone Container said no assurance can be given that any such transaction will be completed or implemented.
